en.greeting: Hi! Today you learn to put a spotlight on the most important part of a sentence, the way Indonesian does with 'yang' and '-lah'. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: One sentence, split in two
steps.text: First: what does 'cleft' mean?
steps.body: **Cleft** = split in two. A **cleft sentence** splits one simple sentence into two parts so that **one part gets the spotlight**. *Sari called* → *It was **Sari** who called*. You already do this in Indonesian: *Sari**-lah yang** menelepon*, ***Yang** saya butuhkan **adalah**…*. Recap: **who** for people, **which** for things, **that** for both. In speech, **stress** the part in focus: *It was **SA**ri who called.*

pairs.en: It was Sari who called.
pairs.id: Sari-lah yang menelepon.

pairs.en: What I need is more time.
pairs.id: Yang saya butuhkan adalah lebih banyak waktu.

pairs.en: All I want is some peace.
pairs.id: Yang saya mau cuma sedikit ketenangan.

steps.title: What-clefts
steps.text: The first pattern puts the spotlight at the end.
steps.body: ***What** + clause + **is/was** + focus.* (A **clause** = a part with its own subject and verb: *I need*, *worries me*.) Here **what** isn't a question: it means *the thing that* (yang). *Yang saya butuhkan **adalah**…* → *What I need **is**…*: **adalah = is**, with **no extra it**. Present → **is**, past → **was**.

pairs.en: What I need is more time.
pairs.id: Yang saya butuhkan adalah lebih banyak waktu.

pairs.en: What worries me is the deadline.
pairs.id: Yang membuat saya khawatir adalah tenggat waktunya.

pairs.en: What I wanted was a window seat.
pairs.id: Yang saya inginkan adalah kursi dekat jendela. (masa lalu → was)

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Watch out for the Indonesian 'adalah' trap.

options: What I really need it is a quiet place to work.
That I really need is a quiet place to work.
What I really need is a quiet place to work.
question.prompt: Rina is working in a noisy co-working space. Which sentence is correct?
question.explanation: What-cleft: **What** + clause + **is** + focus. *adalah* becomes **is**, so there's no extra *it*, and the sentence starts with **what** (*the thing that*), not *that*.

steps.title: More what-clefts
steps.text: Read these. Look at the word after was in the action examples.
steps.body: For an **action**, use *What … **did** was* + the **base verb** (*call*, not *called*), with or without *to*. After a what-clause, **is** is the safe choice, even before a plural noun.

examples.en: What happened was that the server crashed during the demo.
examples.id: Yang terjadi adalah servernya mati saat demo.

examples.en: What we did was call the client straight away.
examples.id: Yang kami lakukan adalah langsung menelepon klien.

examples.en: What she did was to rewrite the whole proposal.
examples.id: Yang dia lakukan adalah menulis ulang seluruh proposal. (to boleh ada)

examples.en: What we need is more staff.
examples.id: Yang kami butuhkan adalah lebih banyak staf. (is: pilihan aman)

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: An action is in focus. Which verb form?

options: send
sent
sending
question.prompt: When the power went off at the office, what we did was ___ everyone home early.
question.explanation: After *What … did was*, use the **base verb**: *send*. *sent* is the past form (the past is already in *did*), and *sending* doesn't follow *did*.

steps.title: It-clefts
steps.text: The second pattern puts the spotlight right after It was.
steps.body: ***It is/It was** + focus + **who/that** + the rest.* A person → **who** or **that**; a thing, time or place → **that**. Great for **correcting a misunderstanding**: *It's **not** the price that worries me, **it's** the delivery time.* Indonesian trap: *Sari-lah **yang**…* → **yang = who/that**, never *she*: *'It was Sari she called me'* ✗.

pairs.en: It was Sari who called, not Budi.
pairs.id: Sari-lah yang menelepon, bukan Budi.

pairs.en: It was in 2021 that we moved to Surabaya.
pairs.id: Justru pada tahun 2021-lah kami pindah ke Surabaya.

pairs.en: It's not the price that worries me, it's the delivery time.
pairs.id: Yang membuat saya khawatir bukan harganya, tapi waktu pengirimannya.

steps.title: Correct the misunderstanding
steps.text: Pak Hasan has the wrong person in mind.

options: No, it was Sari she sent it.
No, it was Sari who sent it.
No, it was the contract that Sari sent.
question.prompt: Pak Hasan: 'So Budi sent the contract to the client?' In fact Sari sent it, not Budi. Which reply corrects Pak Hasan?
question.explanation: The mistake is about the **person**, so the person goes in focus: *It was **Sari who** sent it* (Sari-lah yang mengirim). *she* can't replace *who*, and *the contract* puts the spotlight on the wrong thing.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Put the year in the spotlight.

question.solution: It was in 2019 that we first met.
question.prompt: Arrange the words. The year is the focus: We first met in 2019.
question.explanation: *It was* + the time in focus (*in 2019*) + **that** + the rest (*we first met*). For a time, use **that**, not *who*.

steps.title: All, the thing, the reason
steps.text: Last pattern: like a what-cleft, but the first word adds meaning.
steps.body: **All** = *the only thing* (cuma): *All I want is some peace.* Never *'all what'*: say **All I want** or **All that I want** (Indonesian *semua yang* pushes you to *'all what'*). The same pattern works with **the thing that**, **the reason (why)**, **the place (where)** and **the person who**. In formal writing, *The reason … is **that**…* is safer than *is because*.

pairs.en: All we did was ask a question.
pairs.id: Kami cuma bertanya.

pairs.en: The thing that worries me is the deadline.
pairs.id: Hal yang membuat saya khawatir adalah tenggat waktunya.

pairs.en: The reason I called is that the invoice is wrong.
pairs.id: Alasan saya menelepon adalah tagihannya salah.

pairs.en: The place where we met was a small café in Bandung.
pairs.id: Tempat kami bertemu adalah sebuah kafe kecil di Bandung.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Rina only wants one thing.

options: All I want is to work from home on Fridays.
All what I want is to work from home on Fridays.
All I want it is to work from home on Fridays.
question.prompt: Rina's manager offers her a promotion, a bigger desk and a new laptop. She only wants one thing: to work from home on Fridays. Which sentence is correct?
question.explanation: **All** + clause + **is** + focus = the only thing. After *all*, don't add *what* (*All I want*, or *All that I want*), and don't add *it* before *is*.

steps.text: Here's the whole lesson on one page.

examples.id: Yang kami lakukan adalah langsung menelepon klien.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kamu belajar menyorot bagian terpenting dari sebuah kalimat, seperti yang dilakukan bahasa Indonesia dengan 'yang' dan '-lah'. Yuk, pelan-pelan saja.

steps.title: Satu kalimat, dibelah dua
steps.text: Pertama: apa arti 'cleft'?
steps.body: **Cleft** = terbelah dua. **Cleft sentence** membelah satu kalimat sederhana menjadi dua bagian supaya **satu bagian mendapat sorotan**. *Sari called* → *It was **Sari** who called*. Kamu sudah melakukan ini dalam bahasa Indonesia: *Sari**-lah yang** menelepon*, *Yang saya butuhkan **adalah**…*. Pengingat: **who** untuk orang, **which** untuk benda, **that** untuk keduanya. Saat bicara, **tekan** bagian yang disorot: *It was **SA**ri who called.*

pairs.en: It was Sari who called.
pairs.id: Sari-lah yang menelepon.

pairs.en: What I need is more time.
pairs.id: Yang saya butuhkan adalah lebih banyak waktu.

pairs.en: All I want is some peace.
pairs.id: Yang saya mau cuma sedikit ketenangan.

steps.title: What-cleft
steps.text: Pola pertama menaruh sorotan di bagian akhir.
steps.body: ***What** + bagian kalimat + **is/was** + fokus.* (**Clause** = bagian kalimat dengan subjek dan kata kerja sendiri: *I need*, *worries me*.) Di sini **what** bukan pertanyaan: artinya *hal yang* (yang). *Yang saya butuhkan **adalah**…* → *What I need **is**…*: **adalah = is**, **tanpa it tambahan**. Masa kini → **is**, masa lalu → **was**.

pairs.en: What I need is more time.
pairs.id: Yang saya butuhkan adalah lebih banyak waktu.

pairs.en: What worries me is the deadline.
pairs.id: Yang membuat saya khawatir adalah tenggat waktunya.

pairs.en: What I wanted was a window seat.
pairs.id: Yang saya inginkan adalah kursi dekat jendela. (masa lalu → was)

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Hati-hati dengan jebakan 'adalah'.

options: What I really need it is a quiet place to work.
That I really need is a quiet place to work.
What I really need is a quiet place to work.
question.prompt: Rina bekerja di co-working space yang berisik. Kalimat mana yang benar?
question.explanation: What-cleft: **What** + bagian kalimat + **is** + fokus. *adalah* menjadi **is**, jadi tidak ada *it* tambahan, dan kalimatnya dimulai dengan **what** (*hal yang*), bukan *that*.

steps.title: What-cleft lainnya
steps.text: Baca contoh ini. Perhatikan kata setelah was pada contoh tindakan.
steps.body: Untuk **tindakan**, pakai *What … **did** was* + **kata kerja dasar** (*call*, bukan *called*), boleh dengan atau tanpa *to*. Setelah what-clause, **is** adalah pilihan aman, bahkan sebelum kata benda jamak.

examples.en: What happened was that the server crashed during the demo.
examples.id: Yang terjadi adalah servernya mati saat demo.

examples.en: What we did was call the client straight away.
examples.id: Yang kami lakukan adalah langsung menelepon klien.

examples.en: What she did was to rewrite the whole proposal.
examples.id: Yang dia lakukan adalah menulis ulang seluruh proposal. (to boleh ada)

examples.en: What we need is more staff.
examples.id: Yang kami butuhkan adalah lebih banyak staf. (is: pilihan aman)

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Tindakannya yang disorot. Bentuk kata kerja mana?

options: send
sent
sending
question.prompt: Lengkapi: When the power went off at the office, what we did was ___ everyone home early.
question.explanation: Setelah *What … did was*, pakai **kata kerja dasar**: *send*. *sent* adalah bentuk lampau (masa lalunya sudah ada di *did*), dan *sending* tidak dipakai setelah *did*.

steps.title: It-cleft
steps.text: Pola kedua menaruh sorotan tepat setelah It was.
steps.body: ***It is/It was** + fokus + **who/that** + sisanya.* Orang → **who** atau **that**; benda, waktu atau tempat → **that**. Sangat cocok untuk **meluruskan salah paham**: *It's **not** the price that worries me, **it's** the delivery time.* Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: *Sari-lah **yang**…* → **yang = who/that**, tidak pernah *she*: *'It was Sari she called me'* ✗.

pairs.en: It was Sari who called, not Budi.
pairs.id: Sari-lah yang menelepon, bukan Budi.

pairs.en: It was in 2021 that we moved to Surabaya.
pairs.id: Justru pada tahun 2021-lah kami pindah ke Surabaya.

pairs.en: It's not the price that worries me, it's the delivery time.
pairs.id: Yang membuat saya khawatir bukan harganya, tapi waktu pengirimannya.

steps.title: Luruskan salah pahamnya
steps.text: Pak Hasan mengira orangnya orang lain.

options: No, it was Sari she sent it.
No, it was Sari who sent it.
No, it was the contract that Sari sent.
question.prompt: Pak Hasan: 'So Budi sent the contract to the client?' Padahal Sari yang mengirimnya, bukan Budi. Balasan mana yang meluruskan Pak Hasan?
question.explanation: Salah pahamnya soal **orang**, jadi orangnya yang disorot: *It was **Sari who** sent it* (Sari-lah yang mengirim). *she* tidak bisa menggantikan *who*, dan *the contract* menyorot hal yang salah.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Taruh tahunnya di bawah sorotan.

question.solution: It was in 2019 that we first met.
question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya. Tahunnya yang disorot: Kami pertama kali bertemu pada tahun 2019.
question.explanation: *It was* + waktu yang disorot (*in 2019*) + **that** + sisanya (*we first met*). Untuk waktu, pakai **that**, bukan *who*.

steps.title: All, the thing, the reason
steps.text: Pola terakhir: seperti what-cleft, tapi kata pertamanya menambah arti.
steps.body: **All** = *satu-satunya hal* (cuma): *All I want is some peace.* Jangan *'all what'*: katakan **All I want** atau **All that I want** (*semua yang* dalam bahasa Indonesia mendorongmu ke *'all what'*). Pola yang sama bisa dipakai dengan **the thing that**, **the reason (why)**, **the place (where)** dan **the person who**. Dalam tulisan formal, *The reason … is **that**…* lebih aman daripada *is because*.

pairs.en: All we did was ask a question.
pairs.id: Kami cuma bertanya.

pairs.en: The thing that worries me is the deadline.
pairs.id: Hal yang membuat saya khawatir adalah tenggat waktunya.

pairs.en: The reason I called is that the invoice is wrong.
pairs.id: Alasan saya menelepon adalah tagihannya salah.

pairs.en: The place where we met was a small café in Bandung.
pairs.id: Tempat kami bertemu adalah sebuah kafe kecil di Bandung.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Rina cuma mau satu hal.

options: All I want is to work from home on Fridays.
All what I want is to work from home on Fridays.
All I want it is to work from home on Fridays.
question.prompt: Manajer Rina menawarinya promosi, meja yang lebih besar dan laptop baru. Rina cuma mau satu hal: bekerja dari rumah setiap Jumat. Kalimat mana yang benar?
question.explanation: **All** + bagian kalimat + **is** + fokus = satu-satunya hal. Setelah *all*, jangan tambahkan *what* (*All I want* atau *All that I want*), dan jangan tambahkan *it* sebelum *is*.
